discussion_comments.comment_body: should the taint queue be left around until the debug stream is finished too?

Huh, I thought we didn't taint debug models, but apparently we do, but for typed arrays only, because `emitTypedArrayChunk` can be reached through `serializeDebugTypedArray`. This looks like an accident, all other debug values are not tainted. But maybe they should be? For this PR, I've now moved the clearing of the taint queue back to where it was (after the debug channel is closed).
In prod, we should probably not preserve the original constructor to not leak implementation details.

Follow-up to https://github.com/facebook/react/pull/35810. Doing the same for AggregateError.errors. Since we never serialize them on the Server in prod, we don't need to consider deserializing them in prod on the Client. Also acts as defense-in-depth.

These `hasOwnProperty` checks were the ones that were missing. This is the critical fix. Without it, you can drill into objects not created by the parser itself.

The rest is mainly protecting against other gadgets and to slow down reverse engineering just a bit (which seems to have been somewhat effective especially with llms).

Could this have also been solved by re-creating an object's own properties on a new object with a null prototype? If I'm not missing something, I imagine that would avoid the "shotgun surgery" of ensuring `.hasOwnProperty` guards anywhere which the object's properties are traversed.
